solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time to put up and shut up, almost

parts.note: to put someone up is to quarter or lodge them
a door that is 'to' is pulled closed but not latched, so nearly shut up

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is time to provide lodging and then nearly fall silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' tempts as 'be quiet'; here it is a door pushed to, almost closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifteen minutes before the hour is a time of day, as in 'a quarter to six'.

clue.text: Yard arresting very loud English drunk

indicators.note: a yard arresting something holds it captive within its walls

parts.note: a quad, short for quadrangle, is a college yard
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Police from Scotland Yard detain a noisy, drunken Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard and 'arresting' the police, but the yard is a QUAD that takes in FF and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Having drunk something heartily is to have quaffed it; both are past-tense verbs of swallowing drink.

clue.text: Top class training makes us fit

parts.note: A, as in A1 or grade A, is the top class
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: An elite fitness course gets people into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt and fit are synonyms meaning suitable or appropriate for the purpose.

clue.text: TV set, advanced, with knobs

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase; the answer is used here in its old sense of tuberous, bearing knobbly swellings

parts.note: the tube is slang for the television
rose means went up or advanced

explanation.surface: A description of an old television set with control knobs, moved forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with knobs' reads as part of the TV's description but is the definition: the plant's name comes from its knobbly tubers.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant grows from a knobbly tuber, so its name can describe something tuberous or lumpy.

clue.text: Picks up brown coat leader of hospital body's dropped

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here the one to go
dropped says that front letter is removed from the hospital body

parts.note: an NHS trust is the body running British hospitals; trust's, read as trusts

explanation.surface: Someone collects a brown coat after the head of a hospital board is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: An NHS trust is the organisation that runs a group of British hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that picks up a brown coat of oxidation is corroding, as iron does when it oxidises.

clue.text: Regularly taking position, boy's outside ready

parts.note: someone regularly taking a medicine is said to be on it
a stand is a position taken

indicators.note: the outside of the boy is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boy, regularly taking up a post outside, is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but 'regularly taking' as a whole means ON, as in on medication.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on standby means being ready to act at a moment's notice, a state of preparedness.

clue.text: Brief to raise over a drink

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to cock an ear or a hat is to raise it
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An instruction to lift a drink after a brief toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate made from cocoa powder is a common warm beverage.

clue.text: Rotten egg scoffed? His wasn't all bad

definitions.note: a pronoun phrase pointing to the clergyman of the proverb

parts.note: a bad egg or rotter is a cur, a contemptible person
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: Someone ate a rotten egg; was his meal entirely bad?
explanation.walkthrough: The proverbial curate's egg, from a Punch cartoon, was 'good in parts' as the young clergyman politely told his bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: In the proverb the junior clergyman's breakfast egg was good in parts, so not wholly bad.

clue.text: Fair queen possibly shunning Duke of Wellington and porter

indicators.note: shunning means keeping away from, so the Duke's letter is removed

parts.note: a queen is one example of a playing card
possessive: Wellington's, and a wellington is a boot, giving boot's
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A queen avoids the Duke of Wellington and a hotel porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke of Wellington' reads as one famous man; it splits into D, and Wellington's (a wellington being a rubber boot). A car boot sale is a British market where people sell junk from their car boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is an informal market, a kind of fair where sellers trade from vehicles.

clue.text: One on train fell after receiving large punch

indicators.note: the fell piece, having received the large letter, holds it inside

parts.note: to fell a tree is to axe it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
to box is to punch

explanation.surface: Someone on a train fell over after being punched hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An axlebox is the housing around a railway axle bearing, a component found on every train wheelset.

clue.text: Refurbished front of tourist base in resort

indicators.note: refurbished means done up and rearranged, so the letters are reworked
the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tourist base in a holiday resort has been renovated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refurbished' rearranges T (the front of 'tourist') with BASE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a Riviera town in southern France, a well-known seaside holiday destination.

clue.text: Very little right to be said about sisters

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: concerning or like sisters

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'
R is the short form of right
oral means spoken, to be said rather than written

explanation.surface: There is very little of a sister's rights worth mentioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sororal comes from Latin soror and means relating to or befitting a sister, as fraternal does for brothers.

clue.text: Retriever after day's lost more ground?

indicators.note: lost means taken away, so that letter leaves the retriever

parts.note: a retriever is a finder, one who fetches things
D is the abbreviation for day; 'day's lost' reads as day is lost

explanation.surface: A gun dog, after a day's hunting, has lost more territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retriever' suggests a dog and 'ground' territory; here ground is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Flour or coffee that is ground more is finer, with smaller particles after milling.

clue.text: Spoils were even, say, this time

indicators.note: spoils means ruins or disrupts, so these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The prize money was split evenly, as it happens, on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a noun meaning loot; it is a verb signalling that WERE EVEN SAY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue presents itself as an occasion, and the eve of January 1 is a particular date and time.

clue.text: Sophisticated weapon to burn and fail disastrously

parts.note: to smart is to sting or burn with pain
a show that bombs fails completely

explanation.surface: A high-tech weapon designed to burn things and then misfire badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart bomb is a precision-guided munition, a technologically advanced type of explosive weapon.

clue.text: Daughter has one final letter — the long version — made shorter

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
owns means has or possesses
I is the Roman numeral one
the last letter of the alphabet written out in full in British style

explanation.surface: A daughter's final letter in long form has been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: British English calls the last letter zed, the longer form of the American zee.
explanation.definitionFit: Downsized means reduced in size, often of a company cutting staff, so made smaller or shorter.

clue.text: Raising tip of your sword, strike down Australian park attendant?

indicators.note: in a down clue raising sends everything upward, so it is read from the bottom
here the tip is the far end of the word

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
KO, a knockout, strikes an opponent down
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: Raising your sword's tip, someone fells an Australian park ranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' reverses the lot, as this is a down answer; 'tip of' takes the last letter of 'your', R.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoo is a wildlife park, so someone tending its animals is a kind of park attendant.

clue.text: Underground river no longer flows from the mouth

indicators.note: words that come from the mouth are spoken, so this is how it is pronounced

parts.note: something that sticks has jammed and stops moving

explanation.surface: An underground river has dried up at its estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouth' looks like a river mouth, but it is the speaker's mouth signalling a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Styx is the river of the underworld across which the dead are ferried.

clue.text: Astronaut on reflection best among the stars

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run in reverse
among says the best piece sits within the stars

parts.note: celebrities are names, as in big names
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: On reflection, an astronaut is the best person among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman is a space traveller, the everyday word for an astronaut or cosmonaut.

clue.text: Not exactly cut out for work with canines

parts.note: C is circa, meaning approximately
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone is not quite suited to working with dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out for' looks like an idiom meaning suited to; 'canines' are teeth, not dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing is grinding food with the teeth, and canines are the pointed teeth that help.

clue.text: What's replaced septic tanks, finally?

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so these letters move
finally takes the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A question about what has superseded septic tanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges SEPTIC with S, the last letter of 'tanks'; read whole, the clue describes the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit is a pit for sewage, much like a septic tank, so it could stand in for one.

clue.text: Unusual map is only for those seeking gold?

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an altered arrangement

explanation.surface: A strange map is meant only for prospectors hunting gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests treasure hunters; the gold is a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes at the Games compete for gold medals, so competitors are those seeking gold.

clue.text: Tax period

definitions.meaning: to tax is to strain or push to the limit
a span of time, especially a prison term

explanation.surface: A tax period, as on a form.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain resources is to tax them, and a stint, especially in prison, is a span of time.

clue.text: Fight organisers with issue the cause of weak interaction?

parts.note: the WBO is the World Boxing Organization
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: Boxing promoters and their child cause a lukewarm relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weak interaction' sounds like a feeble relationship; in physics it is the weak nuclear force.
explanation.definitionFit: This particle is one of the carriers of the weak nuclear force in particle physics.

clue.text: Surrounding some bridge, modest collection of plants

indicators.note: surrounding says the modest piece goes around the bridge piece

parts.note: shy means modest or retiring
a rubber is a set of games at bridge

explanation.surface: A modest garden planting surrounds part of a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests a river crossing; it is the card game, where a rubber is a match of three games.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area planted with bushes, so a collection of woody plants.

clue.text: Guy on ornate litter?

definitions.note: a collective noun: a brood of newborn animals

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately worked, so these letters are fancily rearranged

explanation.surface: A man riding on a decorated litter, the carried couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests the ornate carried couch, the palanquin; it is a set of offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a brood of animals born together, and their offspring are collectively called their young.

clue.text: Jump, but don't bounce?

definitions.meaning: to jump over, as a horse does a fence
a cheque that does not bounce goes through the bank

explanation.surface: An instruction to leap but avoid bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse clears a fence by jumping it, and a good cheque clears rather than bouncing.

clue.text: Exercise before small drink

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone does a workout before having a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Press-ups, which Americans call push-ups, are a basic floor exercise.

clue.text: Get down a word in French, the first word penned

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so that word goes inside the French phrase

parts.note: French for 'a word' is un mot
the first word of the French phrase, the article un

explanation.surface: Someone writes down a French word, the first one written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' tempts as written; it means enclosed, the repeated UN going inside UN MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmount is to dismount, as from a horse, so to get down.

clue.text: Something mysterious appearing periodically in outflow

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something strange keeps turning up now and then in a discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: An unidentified flying object is by definition a mysterious thing seen in the sky.

clue.text: SE Asian hotel talked of providing commercial extra

indicators.note: talked of says the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a hotel in Thailand could be a Thai inn

explanation.surface: People talked about a hotel in Southeast Asia that offered a sales bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is promotional merchandise linked to a film or product, a commercial add-on.

clue.text: Chestnut kid keeps in grand Indian dish

indicators.note: keeps in says the chestnut holds the grand letter within it

parts.note: a roan is a horse of chestnut colouring mixed with white
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
to kid is to josh or tease

explanation.surface: A chestnut-haired child stays indoors in a grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnut' suggests a nut or an old joke; here it is a horse's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogan josh is a Kashmiri lamb curry, a staple of Indian restaurant menus.
